topic.subject: science
topic.title: Motion and measurement of distances
topic.scope: standard units, SI units, measuring length correctly, types of motion (straight-line, circular, periodic)

nodes.name: Metre is the SI unit of length
Aligning zero mark with object start

misconceptions.statement: A handspan is a standard unit because everyone has a hand.
misconceptions.why: Students observe that everyone can use their hand to measure and assume the result is universally valid.
misconceptions.fix: Handspans vary in size between different people, so they cannot be used for accurate, universal measurement.

probe.question: If you and your teacher both measure the same table using handspans, will the number of handspans be the same?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because we are both measuring the same table.

misconceptions.statement: 100 cm is longer than 1 metre because 100 is a larger number than 1.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the numerical value rather than the unit scale.
misconceptions.fix: 100 cm and 1 metre represent the exact same physical length; they are just different ways of saying it.

probe.question: Which is longer: a 100 cm stick or a 1 metre stick?

misconceptions.root_belief: a rule from whole numbers works everywhere

misconceptions.statement: If the zero mark of a ruler is broken, you cannot measure anything with it.
misconceptions.why: Students believe the starting point must always be the literal '0' digit on the tool.
misconceptions.fix: You can start from any full mark (like 1 cm) and subtract that value from the final reading.

probe.question: How would you measure a pencil if the first 2 cm of your ruler are broken?
probe.wrong_answer: I cannot use this ruler to get a correct measurement.

misconceptions.statement: It doesn't matter where your eyes are as long as you can see the mark on the ruler.
misconceptions.why: Students do not realize that perspective changes the alignment of the object and the scale.
misconceptions.fix: The eye must be placed vertically above the point where the measurement is to be taken to avoid parallax error.

probe.question: Where should your eye be while taking a reading on a scale?
probe.wrong_answer: Anywhere, as long as I can see the ruler clearly.

misconceptions.statement: A curved line can be measured by placing a straight ruler directly along the curve.
misconceptions.why: Students try to force the tool they have to fit the shape of the object.
misconceptions.fix: A thread is used to trace the curve first, and then the thread's length is measured on a straight ruler.

probe.question: How would you measure the length of a curved snake drawn on paper?
probe.wrong_answer: By keeping the ruler straight over the snake.

misconceptions.root_belief: tools only work for their visual shape

misconceptions.statement: Any motion that is not in a straight line is circular motion.
misconceptions.why: Students overgeneralize the category of 'circular' to include all curves.
misconceptions.fix: Circular motion specifically requires the object to remain at a fixed distance from a center point.

probe.question: Is a car turning a random corner always in circular motion?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it is not going straight.

misconceptions.statement: Motion is only periodic if it happens very fast.
misconceptions.why: Students associate 'repetition' with high frequency or speed, like a vibrating string.
misconceptions.fix: Periodic motion is defined by the regularity of the interval, not the speed; the Earth's orbit is periodic even if it takes a year.

probe.question: Is the movement of the hour hand of a clock periodic?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because it moves too slowly to be repeating.

misconceptions.root_belief: human time scales define physical properties

misconceptions.statement: An object can only have one type of motion at a time.
misconceptions.why: Students find it difficult to decompose complex movements into multiple categories.
misconceptions.fix: Objects can exhibit multiple motions, like a rolling ball which has both rectilinear and circular (rotational) motion.

probe.question: What kind of motion does a sewing machine needle have while the wheel is turning?

misconceptions.root_belief: one object has one single property

misconceptions.statement: A spinning top is in circular motion.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the rotation of an object around its own axis with the circular path of an object around a center.
misconceptions.fix: In circular motion, the whole object moves along a circular path; a spinning top is rotating around an internal axis.

probe.question: If a boy is spinning in one spot, is he in circular motion?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because he is moving in a circle.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: A pendulum's motion is circular because it moves in an arc.
misconceptions.why: Students see the curved path and ignore the repeating back-and-forth nature.
misconceptions.fix: A pendulum is periodic because it repeats its motion along the same path in equal intervals of time.

probe.question: Why is a swinging bell considered periodic motion?
probe.wrong_answer: Because it moves in a circle.

misconceptions.statement: Motion only exists if the object is getting further away from you.
misconceptions.why: Students define motion relative to themselves as the observer rather than a fixed reference point.
misconceptions.fix: Motion is any change in the position of an object with time, regardless of the direction relative to the observer.

probe.question: If a ball is thrown towards you, is it in motion?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because it is coming closer, not going away.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: The SI unit for measuring the distance between cities is the Kilometre.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the 'most common' or 'convenient' unit with the 'standard' (SI) unit.
misconceptions.fix: The SI unit of length is always the Metre; Kilometre is a multiple of the SI unit used for convenience.

probe.question: What is the SI unit of length used to measure the distance between Delhi and Mumbai?
